name: Missive Serif
classification_notes: Art Nouveau-rooted display serif with dramatic flares, gooey ball terminals, and flowing calligraphic-like joins. Tall x-height and narrow proportions suit large-scale graphic applications. Available via Future Fonts as an in-progress release; foundry site lists 5 styles (Light, Medium, Semibold, Bold confirmed).
summary: An ornate Art Nouveau display serif from Portland's Kind Type Foundry, built around dramatic flares, gooey ball terminals, and calligraphic joins.
description: Missive Serif is defined by its highly stylised serif details: dramatic flares, gooey ball terminals, and flowing calligraphic-like joins that draw on Art Nouveau roots. Its tall x-height and narrow proportions make it best suited to graphic, large-scale applications. Released in 2026 by Emily Klaebe via Future Fonts, where it continues to expand toward a full five-style family.
foundry_blurb: Kind Type describe Missive Serif as 'defined by its highly stylized serif details' with 'dramatic flares, gooey ball terminals, and flowing calligraphic-like joins' that allude to its Art Nouveau roots, suited for 'graphic, large-scale applications'.

name: Missive Bead
classification_notes: Grid-based companion to Missive Serif, constructed on a bugle-bead embroidery grid with horizontal, vertical, and 15° diagonal axes. The diagonal axis preserves the calligraphic flow of Missive Serif within the constraints of the bead grid, producing a pixelated-ornate hybrid.
summary: The grid-based sibling of Missive Serif, translating its Art Nouveau forms into a bugle-bead embroidery structure.
description: Missive Bead began as an exploration in translating Missive Serif's ornate forms into beaded embroidery. A grid designed around the proportions of a bugle bead — longer than it is wide — uses three axes (horizontal, vertical, 15° diagonal) to let the calligraphic character of the original survive within the prescribed structure. The result pairs with Missive Serif as a decadently ornate typographic pair.
foundry_blurb: Kind Type describe Missive Bead as 'the outcome of explorations into translating the serif style into beaded embroidery', designed on a bugle-bead grid with a 15° diagonal axis that preserves 'the natural flow of Missive Serif's characteristics'.

name: Francine
classification_notes: Old-style serif foundations with Bauhaus-influenced geometry applied through overweight curves, bulbous ball terminals, and rounded letterforms that push toward the cartoon-esque. Regular, Medium, and Bold function as text weights with hierarchal range; Black is the display weight. Designed during the Type West 2022 programme at Letterform Archive.
summary: A text serif that blends old-style structure with Bauhaus-inflected rounded geometry, landing somewhere between professional and unapologetically graphic.
description: Francine merges old-style serif foundations with Bauhaus geometry: overweight curves, bulbous ball terminals, and rounded letterforms that verge on cartoon-like. Three text weights (Regular, Medium, Bold) give it a working hierarchal range, while the Black weight shifts into display territory. The resulting family sits at the intersection of commercial, pop-culture, and editorial — readable without being restrained. Designed by Emily Klaebe during the Type West 2022 programme at Letterform Archive.
foundry_blurb: Kind Type describe Francine as blending 'the foundations of the old-style genre with influences of rounded traits, infusing Bauhaus-esque geometry through overweight curves, bulbous ball terminals, and rounded letterforms that verge on cartoon-like' — a family that 'balances a professional tone while remaining unapologetically graphic'.
